display.title: Episode 375: Hillel on the Roof and the Invisible Aleph (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Sefiras HaOmer show about loving the Torah: why we learn Pirkei Avos, the story of young Hillel listening on the snowy roof, and the hunt for the invisible aleph.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Sefiras HaOmer, a few days before Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5749. Uncle Yossi explains that the Jewish people counted the days from Egypt to Har Sinai with longing for the Torah, and that we show our love for Torah by learning a chapter of Pirkei Avos each Shabbos, because good midos must come before Torah. A yeshiva boy leads the Shema in Studio 604. Story time tells of the young Hillel, who could not spare the time to gather firewood for the shul and lay on the snowy skylight to hear the Torah being taught, until the students found him nearly frozen and the town freed him from the wood fee. He grew up to be the great Hillel of the Mishnah. Then comes a hunt for the 'invisible aleph': the Torah and every brachah begin with a beis, because the hidden aleph stands for Hashem Echad. A story of the young Frierdiker Rebbe and his teacher shows how to pause before a brachah and think to Whom we are speaking. The show ends with Rosh Chodesh Iyar and Shabbos candle times.
display.lesson: Love the Torah enough to make sacrifices for it, and before every brachah stop and think that you are speaking to Hashem Himself.
